name: Copper Rose
lede: Copper Rose is a muted, grayish pink-red named for the metal copper, recorded in our library by three different systems, most recently Maerz and Paul in 1928.

sections.title: Copper, read as a pink
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[brick-rose]], [[dark-vinaceous]], [[rose-taupe]] and [[marsh-rose]], at 3, 3, 3.5 and 3.5 ΔE [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would class a close match as moderate red, 2.9 units of ΔE away [1].

A near-duplicate swatch in our data, Corinthian Red, sits only 1.9 units off under a different name [1]. A second library color, [[copper-penny]], is built on the same metal word but reads as a browner, less pink shade [1]. In LCH terms Copper Rose is mid-dark and only mildly saturated: lightness 49, chroma 22, hue 22 degrees [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Copper Rose in 112, about 0.5 percent, as photographed [2]. Its fullest appearance is Henri Matisse's *Odalisque with a Screen* of 1923, at 55 percent coverage, and it also appears in an undated Indian work whose own title describes a palette of "mauve, chartreuse and black" [2]. Its use across the archive skews heavily toward Nepal, nearly 51 times the expected rate, and toward India, over 10 times expected, and peaks in the 1920s, in 6 of 237 paintings [2].

origin.source: Maerz and Paul, A Dictionary of Color; Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature; ColorHub library
